text:
ada: Heads-up — EU2 edge dedicated pool (dedicated-eu2-01) had recurring tail latency spikes around 20:10 UTC. Looks correlated to a single tenant (team-lyra) running heavy fp16-TensorRT batches. PCIe util shot up and egress queues backed up.

kai: Any traces/stack dumps? or just telemetry? :thinking:

ada: Mainly telemetry and proxy traces. Short dump attached from the node: ```
node=d0-r3 | pcie_util=0.92 | nvlink_err=0 | kernel_busy_ns=23456789 | kvcache_miss=0.23 | egress_q_depth=147
... repeated every 30s for ~6 mins
```

maria: If PCIe is saturated we can see other tenants hit massive tail latency even if GPU util isn't 100%. Is team-lyra on shared slices or a fractional dedicated carveout?

ada: Shared slices. Their job spikes are bursty (large beam-search runs), so they soak the fabric intermittently.

ops-jen: Proposal: immediate mitigation = soft-route team-lyra to a carved fractional-slice (dedicated-slice-lyra) for the next 2 hours, then backoff. That should contain PCIe churn. Cost impact ~= +12% for that window. Thoughts?

ben: +1 for carveout as short-term. Need an automated rollback if API error rate rises for other tenants. Also warn billing and account owners.

kai: Longer term we should add PCIe and egress-aware routing weights. Right now routing only sees GPU mem/compute. We can include a fabric_score per node (lower is better) and penalize nodes with recent pcie_util > 0.7.

maria: Also add a soft egress throttle at the proxy for large KV-cache priming (prefix loads) — those are often the culprit when combined with TRTexec copies. Small patches to proxy can reduce burst delta by ~40%.

ada: I can run the carveout now. Will flip routing rule to prefer dedicated-slice-lyra for any request with tenant=team-lyra and model_family=trt-* until 21:30 UTC.

sre-bot: [ALERT] EU2-dedicated-eu2-01 tail-latency spike detected x6; mean p95 delta +420ms; linked incident #INC-2026-448.

ops-jen: ada — please capture the exact cost delta and which route rules changed in the change log. Ben — can you coordinate the billing note and get consent from account owner?

ben: On it, pinging acct-eng to approve the short carveout.

kai: Follow-up action items: 1) temporary carveout + rollback job (ada) 2) fabric_score routing change proposal PR (kai) 3) proxy egress-throttle spike mitigation (maria) 4) billing notification + postmortem (ben). Let's aim for PRs + rollback runbook by EOD.

ada: Running carveout now. Will post confirmation when routing converges. :white_check_mark:

ada: Routing converged — team-lyra pinned to dedicated-slice-lyra, observed egress_q_depth drop from 147 -> 18 within two cycles. Monitoring for 15m.

maria: Nice, keep an eye on warmup latency for that tenant (they might see slightly higher steady latency but lower tail).

ben: Billing approved. Notifying account owners.

sre-bot: [RECOVERY] EU2-dedicated-eu2-01 p95 returned to baseline. Incident will be auto-closed in 2h if no regression. :tada:

ada: Postmortem checklist added to #postmortems when incident auto-closes. Will include telemetry snippets and routing diff.

kai: Thanks team. Will start a design doc for fabric-aware routing tomorrow.

maria: Also, let's add a small test harness that simulates TRTexec large-copy bursts against a shared slice to reproduce in staging. That would prevent surprises.

ada: Copy — will add to staging test plan.

ben: Closing loop: short-term carveout succeeded, cost delta within expected range, follow-ups assigned.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from ops-jen, :eyes: from kai)
